sourceOccurrences.label: Finite neighbour sets and finite intrinsic balls
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete grouped source contracts with graph-metric conventions retained
sourceOccurrences.note: 7R5Q covers deterministic bounded-length walk reachability, strict extended-distance balls, the one-root almost-sure finite-neighbour statement, and its simultaneous all-root and all-ball consequences. Countability is used in the probabilistic statements. No uniform row bound or bound below one is assumed. The source proof uses first Borel-Cantelli; the article uses the existing expected-degree identity for the same conclusion. Closed balls at radius zero contain the root, while source open balls at radius zero are empty.

sourceOccurrences.label: Whole-graph events and spanning, Harris and isolation bounds
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete grouped source contracts with empty-vertex and isolation scope
sourceOccurrences.note: POEO distinguishes all-pairs connection from the convention requiring nonempty vertices and gives the measurable global finite/bounded-cluster events. The decreasingness of the latter events is an additional direct consequence. JSS9 retains finite spanning pair sets, finite-vertex Harris products and the countable isolation upper bound with another vertex required. It reuses UNJ6 for the isolation identity/product. The finite spanning hypothesis itself forces finite vertices, explaining the absence of a separate countability assumption. No source error or compiled tag association is asserted.

proofUses.reason: Finite-neighbour induction gives finite-radius balls; finite degree expectation and a countable intersection give simultaneous almost-sure local finiteness.
Global events are countable intersections of connection or volume events; adding edges preserves connections and enlarges clusters.
A spanning cylinder and Harris give lower bounds. Global connection excludes isolation when another vertex exists, and the isolation product supplies the finite upper bound.
